title: DeepSeek API for coding agents: direct integration vs Weave Router
summary: Compare direct DeepSeek API setup with Weave Router for coding agents, including API formats, per-action routing, pricing, caching and quality evidence.
body_markdown:
The DeepSeek API lets a coding agent call DeepSeek models directly. Weave Router adds a different capability: it selects a model and provider for each action your agent takes, so you can use DeepSeek alongside frontier models in the same workflow.


Use direct access when you want to choose a DeepSeek model explicitly and pay DeepSeek for its API usage. Use Weave Router when you want model selection across an approved pool, coding-agent setup, and a record of which model served each request. The useful comparison is the cost and quality of completed coding work.


API details and prices checked November 3, 2026.


## Weave's published cost and quality evidence


Weave's[Router 2.0 evaluation](https://weaveos.com/blog/introducing-weave-router-2-0) reports Astra quality at about half the cost and more than twice the speed on two agentic coding benchmarks. Router and GPT-6 Astra used the same Codex harness and tasks, with two attempts per task in paired runs.


Scroll horizontally if needed →


Benchmark Tasks Router / Astra tasks solved Router / Astra cost per trial Router / Astra mean time per trial


Terminal-Bench 4.0 66 62.1% / 60.6% $5.22 / $10.03 20.5 / 44.1 minutes


SWE-Atlas Codebase QnA 124 62.1% / 66.1% $2.31 / $5.04 6.8 / 16.7 minutes


Tasks solved is pass@2: a task counts when either attempt passes. Cost and time are per trial. The published comparison is Router versus GPT-6 Astra; it does not establish the result of a direct DeepSeek comparison.


That is the reason to evaluate routing on finished work. A token-price table describes the price of a model call. These results measure whether an agent completes a coding task, what its attempts cost, and how long they take. The[published methodology](https://weaveos.com/router/benchmark-methodology) makes the comparison inspectable.


## Send a direct DeepSeek API request


DeepSeek's[official quickstart](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/) uses` https://api.deepseek.com` for OpenAI-format requests. Its current API model IDs are` deepseek-flash` and` deepseek-v4-pro` .


With your DeepSeek API key already set in` DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` , this Bash example requests a small Python change:


```text
curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
'https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions' \
-H "Authorization: Bearer ${DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}" \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-binary @- <<'JSON'
{
"model": "deepseek-flash",
"messages": [
{
"role": "user",
"content": "Write a Python mean(values) function that returns 0 for an empty list. Include two unit tests."
}
],
"thinking": { "type": "enabled" },
"reasoning_effort": "high",
"stream": false
}
JSON


```


Read the generated answer in` choices\[0\].message.content` . This request returns suggested code. A coding agent also needs to apply edits, execute tools, and run tests in your repository.


For a custom tool loop, follow DeepSeek's[Chat Completions contract](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/api/create-chat-completion/) and[thinking-mode guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode/) . Thinking mode is enabled by default. It rejects` required` and named` tool_choice` values, and requests that carry tools must retain the required` reasoning_content` in later messages. A successful text-only request does not exercise that tool loop.


## Connect Claude Code or Codex


DeepSeek documents direct integrations for both clients. You can choose the service first, then follow its client-specific setup.


Scroll horizontally if needed →


Coding agent Direct DeepSeek setup Weave Router setup


Claude Code[DeepSeek's Claude Code guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/agent_integrations/claude_code/) uses its Anthropic-compatible endpoint and a DeepSeek key` npx @weave-os/router --claude` configures the client for Weave


Codex[DeepSeek's Codex guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/agent_integrations/codex/) uses its native Responses API and a DeepSeek model catalog` npx @weave-os/router --codex` configures the client for Weave


DeepSeek's Claude Code guide also documents model-name mapping. Claude Opus names select DeepSeek Pro; Claude Haiku and Sonnet names select DeepSeek Flash. Check the served model when comparing costs.


Weave's[managed setup guide](https://docs.weaveos.com/router/getting-started) requires Node.js 18 or later, an organization-issued router key, and the credits, subscriptions, or provider keys appropriate to your plan. The installer handles the coding client's configuration. Self-hosting is a separate deployment path in the[Router README](https://github.com/weave-os/router/blob/2f0781ae3b94590dd9ec37dea4ed25880299fbac/README.md#run-it-yourself) .


Keep the credentials distinct. A DeepSeek key authenticates to DeepSeek. A Weave router key authenticates to Weave. For routed DeepSeek models, confirm the enabled model and its upstream provider in your Router configuration. The[provider reference](https://github.com/weave-os/router/blob/2f0781ae3b94590dd9ec37dea4ed25880299fbac/docs/CONFIGURATION.md) documents OpenRouter and other OpenAI-compatible endpoints; the[custom-endpoint guide](https://docs.weaveos.com/router/custom-endpoints) explains provider bindings and model aliases.


## What per-action routing changes


A coding session contains many model requests. Reading a file, interpreting a tool result, proposing a patch, and responding to a failed test can each lead to another request with a different amount of work to do.


Weave's[routing semantics](https://github.com/weave-os/router/blob/2f0781ae3b94590dd9ec37dea4ed25880299fbac/docs/SEMANTICS.md) define an **action** as one upstream API request to a model. That is the routing grain. One agent turn can contain several actions. Session state and explicit model pins can influence each decision; per-action routing does not mean switching models on every request.


This gives Weave a useful role even when DeepSeek is already part of your stack:


- **Use more than one model without changing coding clients.** Keep DeepSeek in the eligible pool alongside the other models your organization enables.
- **Control the choices.** Weave's[models and routing controls](https://docs.weaveos.com/router/models-and-routing) let you exclude models or providers, set preferences, and pin a session when you want a specific model.
- **Inspect the work behind the bill.**[Router reporting](https://docs.weaveos.com/router/reporting) connects requests to serving models, token counts, costs, users, and sessions. Decision exports provide the underlying rows for your own analysis.


The agent executes local tools. Router selects the upstream model. For example, a request that produces a file-read tool call and the next request carrying that file's contents are separate routing actions, even though they belong to the same task.

Decision Direct DeepSeek API Weave Router

DeepSeek API model IDs and Router catalog IDs are different namespaces. Record the exact served model and provider on both paths before treating two runs as a model-for-model comparison.


## DeepSeek API pricing


These are DeepSeek's published direct API rates, checked November 3, 2026. All values are **USD per one million tokens** , shown as **off-peak / peak** . The[official pricing page](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing/) is the source of truth.


Scroll horizontally if needed →


API model Cached input Uncached input Output


` deepseek-flash` $0.003 / $0.006 $0.15 / $0.30 $0.60 / $1.20


` deepseek-v4-pro` $0.022 / $0.044 $0.66 / $1.32 $1.98 / $3.96


Peak windows are 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday, excluding Chinese public holidays. The current` deepseek-flash` alias serves DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017; the Pro version is DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813. DeepSeek also lists Search and Fetch separately at $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests for each API. Include those charges when your agent uses those services.


Your effective cost depends on input/output mix, cache hits, reasoning, retries, and tool loops.[DeepSeek caching](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/kv_cache/) is enabled by default, but hits depend on matching persisted prefixes. Use returned usage rather than assuming the whole repository context is cached.


These direct rates are not a Weave invoice estimate. Use the actual upstream and[Weave billing terms](https://docs.weaveos.com/router/billing) for your selected path. Keep the estimate date with your budget because provider rates and model aliases change.


## Compare the two paths on your repository


Start with direct DeepSeek as an explicit baseline, then compare it with Weave Router using the same coding agent, task mix, acceptance tests, and review standard. Record the exact model versions and reasoning settings. Include failed attempts and retries in both groups.


Scroll horizontally if needed →


Measure What to record


API spend Input/output usage, cache hits, tool charges, retries, and the actual billed cost


Task completion Whether the requested change passes the same acceptance criteria


Latency Time to first token and time to a completed, accepted change


Code quality Review findings, post-merge defects, and follow-up work


PR keep rate The same retention definition and follow-up window for both groups


Cost per merged PR Total spend on all attempts divided by merged PRs in the tested work


Use Router's serving-model and session records to inspect its choices, then connect those sessions to your work items. Its dashboard's savings comparison uses the configured comparison model; a direct DeepSeek pilot needs a matched direct baseline as well.


## Choose the path that matches your workload


Choose direct DeepSeek when you want an explicit DeepSeek integration with one provider's API and billing. Choose Weave Router when your coding workflow benefits from selecting among DeepSeek and other enabled models per action, with coding-client setup and centralized routing controls.


**[Set up Weave Router](https://weaveos.com/router/quickstart)** and compare the resulting model mix, spend, and completed work with your direct baseline.


## Frequently asked questions


### Can Claude Code and Codex use DeepSeek directly?


Yes. DeepSeek publishes client-specific guides for Claude Code through its Anthropic-compatible endpoint and Codex through its Responses API. Use the current guide for your client rather than reusing another client's configuration.


### Can Weave select a different model within one agent turn?


Yes. Its documented routing grain is one upstream API request, and an agent turn can contain several requests. Session pins and deployment policy still affect which model is selected.


### Does Weave Router provide DeepSeek's official API?


They are separate services. DeepSeek operates its direct API. Weave Router selects models and providers for supported agent requests, including enabled DeepSeek routes in your configuration.


### Can I compare DeepSeek's token rate with Router's benchmark cost?


They measure different things. The pricing table is USD per million direct API tokens. The benchmark reports cost per trial on a stated task set. Compare both paths using the same tasks and include all attempts before drawing a cost conclusion.
